text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said Slovakia would abolish its import deposit scheme immediately after the Czech Republic does so.
- Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said the government did not agree with the state-run electricity monopoly Slovenske Elektrarne on an increase in electric energy prices.

- Slovakia's largest largest medical equipment maker Chirana Prema a.s. said it had won a $3 million contract financed by the World Bank in Belarus. Chirana said it would submit its bid in a similar tender in Romania.
- The turmoil with the Czech crown last week has not so far significantly affected the Slovak crown.

PRAVDA - Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik said Slovakia still had a chance to become a NATO member in the first wave of its eastward enlargement, but he added that if this did not happen Bratislava should be integrated in the alliance in future expansion rounds.
- Hamzik said he believed the forthcoming referendum on NATO membership will be successful with sufficient turnout and enough people voting in favour of the integration.
- Premier Meciar said he did not want to become Slovak President.

- Meciar's ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) said it would propose an earlier date for the general election in 1998. HZDS said the elections should take place at the beginning of June instead of the originally scheduled September.
SME - The Slovak National Party (SNS), a minor member of the ruling coalition, said membership in NATO will endanger Slovakia's independence and sovereignity.
- SNS Chairman Jan Slota will meet U.S. ambassador to Slovakia Ralph Johnson on Monday to ask the U.S. administration to guarantee Slovakia's military neutrality.
- Peter Mihok, Chairman of the Slovak Trade and Industry Chamber, said delays in Bratislava's integration with the European Union will be dangerous for Slovakia's economy.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The state-run postal monopoly, Slovenska Posta (SP), plans to invest around one billion crowns in development projects within the next five years. The SP said it planned to issue a 400 million crown tranche of five year domestic bonds.
